angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 619,173 km at 117.07 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.5423 +/- 0.0184 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 117.07 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.89 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Castro-González et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1839 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract): 619,173 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.86 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Castro-González et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1839 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5347 +/- 67 K from Castro-González et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1839 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Castro-González et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1839 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1839.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.474, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1839 (pscomppars): spectral type G9 V, from Castro-González et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1839 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.09 dex, from Castro-González et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1839 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.264, from Castro-González et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1839 (pscomppars): age 4.1 Gyr, from Castro-González et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1839 (pscomppars): rotation period 24 d, from Castro-González et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1839 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.4 km/s, from Castro-González et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260905413C/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.89 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.746. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
